# Get-ADUserLogonComputer

<!-- Generated by tools/Build-Catalog.ps1. Edit the script header, not this file. -->

Finds which computers a user has authenticated from, using domain controller Security logs.

| | |
|---|---|
| Location | `scripts/windows/active-directory/Get-ADUserLogonComputer.ps1` |
| Platform | Windows (RSAT ActiveDirectory module) |
| Permissions | Event Log Readers (or Domain Admin) on every domain controller |
| Safety | Read-only |

## When to use

Investigating an account lockout source, a suspected compromised account, or "where is this user logged in".

## Description

Queries every domain controller for Security events 4624 (logon), 4768 (Kerberos TGT) and 4769 (Kerberos
service ticket) for the given user over the last N days. Results are grouped per device with hit count, last
seen time and source IPs, and exported to CSV. IP-only entries are resolved to host names where DNS allows.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-User` | String | Yes | sAMAccountName of the user to trace. |
| `-Days` | Int32 | No | How many days back to search. Default 7. Large values on busy DCs can be slow, and the Security log must still hold the events. |
| `-OutputPath` | String | No | Folder for the CSV. Falls back to $env:TOOLBOX_REPORT_DIR, then prompts. |
| `-CustomerName` | String | No | Optional. Adds a &lt;OutputPath&gt;\&lt;CustomerName&gt; subfolder. |
| `-GridView` | SwitchParameter | No | Also open the results in Out-GridView (interactive Windows sessions only). |

## Examples

```powershell
.\Get-ADUserLogonComputer.ps1 -User jsmith -Days 14 -OutputPath D:\Reports
```

```powershell
.\Get-ADUserLogonComputer.ps1 -User jsmith -OutputPath D:\Reports -CustomerName Contoso -GridView
```
